title: At-Tariq 86:13-17 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Summer 1: At-Tariq 9 to 17, Al-Burooj 1 to 11 and stopping signs
source: Written for quran/y5 lesson 33 (Pupil PDF worksheet: At-Tariq 86:13-17 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 33. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: إِنَّهُۥ لَقَوْلٌۭ فَصْلٌۭ (١٣) وَمَا هُوَ بِٱلْهَزْلِ (١٤) إِنَّهُمْ يَكِيدُونَ كَيْدًۭا (١٥) وَأَكِيدُ كَيْدًۭا (١٦) فَمَهِّلِ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ أَمْهِلْهُمْ رُوَيْدًۢا (١٧)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Indeed, the Qur'an is a decisive statement,
Indeed, they are planning a plan,
But I am planning a plan.
So allow time for the disbelievers. Leave them awhile.

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Ghunnah on نّ; izhar shafawi before ي
Stopping on fathatan at the end of the surah

questions.q: Chunk and link At-Tariq 86:13-17 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 86:13-17 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 86:13-17 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Recite At-Tariq 1 to 17 to a partner.
What do 86:15 to 17 teach about patience?
questions.a: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to give the disbelievers time: Allah's plan is greater than any plot.
A) a decisive word, not amusement. 86:13 to 14.

questions.q: At-Tariq 86:15: «إِنَّهُمْ يَكِيدُونَ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Allah says the Qur'an is a decisive word, not a joke (86:13 to 14). How should we behave when the Qur'an is being recited?
questions.a: Listen quietly and respectfully; it is serious, true speech from Allah.
